gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Apple's 18-hour battery rating for the Apple Watch SE 3 GPS + Cellular assumes only 4 hours on cellular and 14 hours paired to an iPhone over Bluetooth. That is 4 / 18 = 22% of the rated day on cellular, so a day with no phone nearby falls outside the condition Apple rated.
standout_why: I compared against the cited support.apple.com/en-us/119601 (Set up cellular on Apple Watch) and the cited samsung.com/ca 'Set up your Galaxy Watch with or without a phone' page, plus the uncited apple.com/apple-watch-for-your-kids. Apple's cellular page only says 'Turning on cellular for extended periods uses more battery power' and gives no hours. Samsung's page has no battery figures. The kids page states no battery life or cellular runtime. None of them says how much of the rated battery day was spent on cellular. Our current page also shows '18 h' for the SE 3 with no duty-cycle caveat.
decides: This confirms the SE 3 as the iPhone-side pick but changes how its battery cell should read: '18 h (rated with 4 h on cellular, 14 h near an iPhone)', not a bare 18 h for a no-phone day. Samsung's own page also contradicts our Galaxy Watch row: Wear OS models (Galaxy Watch4 and later) need a compatible phone for the first setup, so 'Samsung allows standalone setup on LTE models' is wrong and must change to 'Yes, an Android phone'. Samsung US now sells the Galaxy Watch9, so the Watch8 row may be out of date.

findings.label: Rated all-day battery and its test duty cycle
findings.value: Up to 18 h, of which 4 h on cellular and 14 h connected to iPhone via Bluetooth
findings.note: Apple's test: 300 time checks, 90 notifications, 15 min app use, 60-min workout with Bluetooth music playback from the watch, over 18 h. Pre-production hardware, tested July–August 2025.

findings.label: Share of the rated battery day spent on cellular (derived)
findings.note: 4 h cellular / 18 h rated day = 0.22. The other 78% (14 h) assumes a paired iPhone nearby. Apple gives no rating for a day spent entirely on cellular.

findings.label: Apple's cellular battery caveat
findings.value: 'Turning on cellular for extended periods uses more battery power' (no hours given)
findings.source_title: Set up cellular on Apple Watch - Apple Support
findings.note: This is the page ChatGPT cited. It also says the iPhone and watch must be on the same carrier unless the watch is set up with Apple Watch For Your Kids, and that pre-paid plans aren't currently supported.

findings.label: US starting price for the SE 3 line
findings.note: This is the line's starting price. The page did not show the separate GPS + Cellular 40mm price.

findings.label: Setup without a phone
findings.value: Not possible: Wear OS models (Galaxy Watch4 and later) require a compatible phone for initial setup
findings.source_title: Set up your Galaxy Watch with or without a phone | Samsung CA
findings.note: Phone-free setup is limited to Galaxy Watch, Watch Active, Active2 and Watch3. After setup, LTE Wear OS models can stay connected on mobile data without the phone. Wear OS models are not compatible with iOS.

findings.label: Samsung US store price (Bluetooth 40mm)
findings.note: The page showed no separate 40mm LTE price.

findings.label: Battery capacity and Samsung's runtime statement
findings.value: 390 mAh; up to 30 h with AOD, about 40 h without AOD
findings.note: The runtime is from a Samsung customer-service reply on its own store page, not a spec footnote, and states no LTE duty cycle. Shows that the Watch9 has replaced the Watch8 as Samsung's current model.

findings.label: Apple Watch For Your Kids compatible models
findings.value: Recommends SE 3 GPS + Cellular; Series 4 and later with cellular also work
findings.source_title: Apple Watch For Your Kids - Apple
findings.note: No battery, cellular runtime or plan price on the page ('Check with your carrier').
